correctness.rationale: The power-domination condition is a terminating monotone unique-unobserved-neighbor closure; both programs exhaust all subsets up to size four and find no solutions of size at most three and exactly 6,540 successful four-sets. The duad–syntheme incidence model and independently coded 4-bit symplectic incidence model are explicitly isomorphic by an edge-checked 30-vertex mapping. Move construction enumerates every possible one-vertex substitution, and for slides requires an original graph edge. The Python checker verifies 1,440 distinct induced automorphisms and ten exhaustive orbits, computes exact shortest paths from every orbit representative and weights the shells; the independent C++ verifier computes all pairs directly from all 6,540 states. Edge counts, eccentricity distributions, shortest-distance histograms, and all ten locality-penalty counts agree. A printed thirteen-slide path is witnessed and BFS proves it shortest. No infinite inference is used.

value.rationale: For the canonical unique 30-vertex cubic graph of girth eight, the exact shape and mobility of minimum four-sensor observation states is a natural and motivated graph-algorithm benchmark. Both relocation modes remain connected, yet physically adjacent sliding has radius eleven and diameter thirteen while arbitrary replacement has diameter four. Precisely 1,440 pairs pay the sharp additional nine moves, and the full distribution and ten symmetry types explain that worst-case difference. The result is an exact finite invariant and meaningful algorithmic stress test, without unsupported claims of generalized theory.
